name: bulk-transform
description: Same mechanical transformation over a DECLARED roster, applied lane-by-lane and audited against the roster. TEACHES FOUR SURFACES: (1) fan-out with a STATIC items list where each item carries its own goal (no {item} template needed); (2) the barrier (NO quorum) for a coverage job - every lane must answer or the audit names it; (3) an ancestor `inputs:` ref - the audit reads the manifest echo (a grandparent) explicitly, not via auto-injection; (4) deterministic self-verification: every lane must name the command+output that PROVES its transform landed - a claimed change without an observing command is a failed lane. Seed (run_context map): 'work_root' = a directory holding the files to transform (this example normalizes each listed file's name to lowercase and appends a stamped trailer line). The roster echo is the master manifest: the audit reconciles all_results against it and may NEVER claim more than it names.  CONTRACT-vs-COVERAGE reading law: the fan-out header's failed_items counts CONTRACT failures only (lanes that answered their schema), so an honest applied:false is a committed answer and keeps failed_items at 0 - turning that honest negative into a named coverage gap against the manifest is the AUDIT'S job, not an engine signal. A reader who confuses the two will misdiagnose the engine instead of reading the roster. Adapt items + the transform goal to your real fleet (renames, config migrations, format bumps).

defaults.context:
You are one lane of a bulk-transform workflow. Ground rules:
- Touch ONLY the file named in your item goal, inside the declared work root. No other writes.
- Self-report is not proof: your evidence field must carry a command you ran and what it printed (e.g. `ls` of the new name, `tail -1` of the trailer).
- If the source file does not exist or the transform cannot be applied, say so honestly as applied=false with the reason - never simulate success and never create substitute files.
- Reply with ONLY one fenced ```json block as your final message.

output.note: master manifest - the audit reconciles against THIS list; anything not named here did not exist for this run, and anything here with no lane answer is a named gap.

items.goal: In the work root {run.work_root}: rename the file 'Alpha.cfg' to lowercase 'alpha.cfg', then append the single trailer line 'normalized-by: bulk-transform' to it. Prove with ls of alpha.cfg and tail -1. Reply ONLY fenced json {"file": "alpha.cfg", "applied": true|false, "evidence": "<command + what it printed>"}

In the work root {run.work_root}: rename the file 'beta-report.cfg' to 'beta_report.cfg' (dash to underscore), then append the single trailer line 'normalized-by: bulk-transform' to it. Prove with ls of beta_report.cfg and tail -1. Reply ONLY fenced json {"file": "beta_report.cfg", "applied": true|false, "evidence": "<command + what it printed>"}

In the work root {run.work_root}: rename the file 'GAMMA.cfg' to 'gamma.cfg', then append the single trailer line 'normalized-by: bulk-transform' to it. Prove with ls of gamma.cfg and tail -1. Reply ONLY fenced json {"file": "gamma.cfg", "applied": true|false, "evidence": "<command + what it printed>"}

nodes.goal: Reconcile the transform results (## Inputs: the fan-out payloads) against the master manifest (labelled roster - you receive it explicitly because it is a grandparent, not a direct parent). For EVERY manifest name: was there a lane answer, did it claim applied, does its evidence name an observing command? Independently spot-check the work root {run.work_root} yourself with ls - list what actually exists. The answer must name the incomplete set exactly when anything is missing, failed, or unsupported by evidence - never report a full roster you cannot see. Reply ONLY fenced json {"complete": true|false, "per_file": ["<manifest name>: applied|failed|no-answer — evidence verdict"], "discrepancies": ["<what the filesystem shows that the lanes did not report, or 'none'>"], "verdict": "<one line the owner reads first>"}
